summary: Proposes AC-OPD, an on-policy distillation variant in which the teacher continues for an adaptively chosen number of tokens from selected anchor points in student rollouts, motivated by an observed 'teacher uncertainty contraction' and a variance-bias bound. Evaluated by distilling Qwen3-4B->1.7B and Qwen3-32B->4B on math (AMC/AIME/Minerva) and code (HumanEval+/MBPP+).

claims.claim: AC-OPD improves over standard OPD by 4.37 points Math Avg. and 3.50 points Code Avg.
claims.evidence: Table 1 Setting 1: OPD 33.65/57.70 vs AC-OPD 38.03/61.20. Setting 2 gains are smaller: Math 47.78->50.38, Code 75.60->76.65 (+1.05). Headline numbers are the larger setting only. OPD baseline AIME24 13.3 in Setting 1 is far below SFT's 23.0, suggesting a weak baseline run.

claims.claim: Results are robust over five independent runs.
claims.evidence: Table 1 reports std devs of 0.09-0.46pp, including on AIME24/25 (30 problems each, ~3.3pp per problem); such small spreads across independent training runs are implausible without explanation of what varies across runs.

claims.claim: Adaptive continuation length beats fixed lengths and a shuffled control.
claims.evidence: Table 3 (Setting 1 code only): Adaptive 61.20 vs Fixed-8 60.85 (+0.35) vs Shuffled 60.10 vs Fixed-6 58.45. Margin over best fixed policy is within noise for HumanEval+ (164 problems).

claims.claim: Gains are not from extra supervised tokens.
claims.evidence: Figure 5: early-stage training only, code task only, matched supervised tokens; no numbers in text.

patterns.note: Model-training method (distillation) for small students; no agentic or tool-use setting evaluated.

methodology.sample: Math: AMC23, AIME24, AIME25, Minerva (pass@16); Code: HumanEval+, MBPP+ (pass@1).
methodology.baselines: SFT, OPD, ExOPD, EOPD (recent 2026 variants); all same protocol.
methodology.variance: Mean ± std over five runs reported, but magnitudes look implausibly small for 30-problem benchmarks.
methodology.ablations: Anchor selection, fixed vs adaptive horizon, shuffled control, token-matched early training — all on Setting 1 code only.
methodology.contamination_controls: None discussed; HumanEval+/MBPP+/AMC are widely exposed benchmarks.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; no venue in comment or journal_ref.
standards.artifacts: Code 'will be made publicly available upon publication'; none released.

biases.detail: Only the Qwen3 family as teacher and student.
Function-level HumanEval+/MBPP+ for code; no repository or agentic tasks.
Setting 1 OPD AIME24 score (13.3) is 10 points below SFT (23.0), inflating the headline Math gain; no tuning details for baselines.
Public benchmarks with no contamination analysis.

coi.affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Automation, CAS; Ant Group (first author was an Ant Group intern; per-author mapping beyond that is not given in the text).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None; Qwen3 (Alibaba) used as base models, not an Ant product.
coi.detail: Industry co-affiliation (Ant Group) but no proprietary product evaluated.

verdict_reason: off-topic: a method for distilling LLM weights on math and Python function-level benchmarks, with nothing about agents, harnesses or software-engineering workflows. Its evidence is also thin: the headline gains come from the smaller-scale setting, the OPD baseline looks weak, std devs are implausibly small and no code is released.
applicability: None for the Java healthcare-education ingestion team. They consume hosted models through mixed agent hosts and will not train or distill student models, and nothing here touches multi-repo ingestion, spec-driven development or harness design.
